summary.text: A 53-year-old male with no significant past medical history and no diagnosis of diabetes mellitus presented with a progressive four-month history of left-sided otorrhea, otalgia, and retro- and preauricular pain after prior amoxicillin/clavulanic acid had not helped. Examination showed signs of cutaneous infection, bone erosion of the external auditory canal and foul-smelling otorrhea, and he was admitted with a presumptive diagnosis of malignant otitis externa.

Initial laboratory results showed leukocytosis of 20,050 cells/μL, a normal glucose of 91 mg/dL, elevated C-reactive protein, non-reactive VDRL and HIV tests, negative blood and fungal cultures, and an ear secretion culture that identified Proteus mirabilis with a listed resistance and sensitivity pattern. MRI on the third hospital day and CT showed mastoid cell occupation, an external auditory canal lesion and bone erosion, and carcinoma was considered and excluded.

Intravenous piperacillin/tazobactam 4.5 g every 6 h was started based on culture sensitivity with dexamethasone, diclofenac and paracetamol, and purulent material was repeatedly aspirated and granulation tissue and necrotic debris debrided. After 7 days leukocytes fell to 11,700 cells/μL; he stayed 17 days with consistent improvement and was discharged on oral ciprofloxacin and omeprazole for a three-month antibiotic course, under multidisciplinary management with otorhinolaryngologists and infectious disease specialists.

At the three-month follow-up he showed substantial clinical improvement, repeat otoendoscopy was described as near-complete resolution, and the follow-up image showed a dry ear without purulent discharge. Monitoring was ongoing to ensure full recovery and prevent recurrence, and the abstract reports clinical resolution without recurrence.
